tagline: Delivering Energy and Essential Services to Communities
hero_kpi_rationale: Adjusted gross margin is a key indicator of the company's operational profitability, demonstrating its ability to cover direct costs of energy production and distribution. For a utility company, strong gross margin is essential to finance necessary infrastructure investments and ensure operational sustainability.

kpis.name: Adjusted Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Non-GAAP measure calculated by deducting the cost of natural gas, propane, and electricity purchases as well as direct labor costs of revenue-generating activities from operating revenue. Excludes depreciation and certain operating and maintenance costs.
kpis.description: Adjusted gross margin represents the direct profitability of the company's energy distribution activities after accounting for direct production and labor costs.
kpis.signal: Strong and stable adjusted gross margin, indicative of efficient direct cost management.

kpis.name: Capital Expenditures
kpis.explanation: Total amount of funds used to acquire or improve long-term physical assets, notably natural gas and electricity distribution infrastructure.
kpis.description: Capital expenditures are critical to maintaining and developing utility infrastructure, ensuring reliability, safety, and future operational capacity.
kpis.signal: Sustained investments in network maintenance, safety, and energy infrastructure expansion.

kpis.name: Total Headcount
kpis.explanation: Total number of employees working for the company across all operating segments.
kpis.description: Employee count is an indicator of operational scale and workforce requirements for managing energy distribution operations.
kpis.signal: Stable headcount appropriate to the nature of energy utility operations.

risks.title: Cyberattacks Disrupting Operations
risks.score_rationale: Risk is explicitly mentioned in risk factors and reinforced by a dedicated Item 1C on cybersecurity. Language indicates elevated risk of operational disruption and loss of sensitive data. Highly critical category for utilities.

risks.title: Increased Safety Regulation
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned in general risk factors with concerned language regarding growing federal, state, and local regulation. Potentially high impact on operating costs and operational standards.

risks.title: Dependence on Capital Markets
risks.score_rationale: Risk is repeated in risk factors and in the Safe Harbor section. Financing of growth strategy depends on access to credit markets. Language emphasizes economic conditions and credit ratings.

risks.title: Complex Acquisition Integration
risks.score_rationale: Acquisition integration risk is mentioned in risk factors and illustrated by the recent FCG acquisition for $922.8 million. Integration failure could impact profitability.

risks.title: Energy Demand Variability
risks.score_rationale: Factor is mentioned in macroeconomic risks. Depends on economic conditions, customer preferences, and weather patterns. Less critical than others but recurring.

risks.title: Competition from Energy Suppliers
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned in general risk factors. Risk of losing customers to other suppliers or alternative energy sources exists but is mitigated by the regulated nature of core operations.

risks.title: Tax Change Risks
risks.score_rationale: Cited in risk factors with explicit reference to TCJA. Tax changes can significantly impact profitability and cash flows. Language emphasizes meaningful risk.
